headline: Mechanistic models infer gene networks and perturbation responses from omics data
label: Mechanistic Modeling Of Biological Networks
summary: New methods couple mechanistic structure with statistical inference for single-cell, microbiome, and multi-omic datasets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the incorporation of mechanistic or distributional structure into statistical inference on omics data. RI-SINDy removes known Hill-type regulatory terms from SINDy regressions and recovers their coefficients through a drift-balance condition, improving conditioning. CardamomOT jointly infers gene regulatory networks, unobserved protein trajectories, and cell trajectories within an optimal transport framework. Latent causal diffusion models single-cell expression as a noisy stationary diffusion to predict unseen perturbation responses. PRISM applies empirical Bayes inverse-Wishart estimation to sample-specific covariance networks from cross-sectional and longitudinal data, while joint mTobit separates structural zeros from latent microbial abundance in zero-inflated microbiome data. Archetypal analysis extends likelihood-based modeling to binary, count, and categorical data. The new element is explicit modeling of known regulation, sample heterogeneity, or zero inflation rather than generic fitting.
